subject: Clarify: on-prem failback SLA & customer maintenance windows
messages:
From: Ops Team (Radial Bio) <ops@radial.bio>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Scheduled maintenance windows + failback expectations

Hi David,

We're getting ready to publish our quarterly maintenance calendar for the private colo that hosts your customer's tenant. The operations team will run rolling host-level reboots and patching across their racks during the windows below: 2027-04-02 02:00-06:00 UTC and 2027-04-16 02:00-06:00 UTC.

A couple of ask items from our side before we publish to our change board:
- Can Redwood confirm whether a hosted fallback (failback to Redwood-hosted fallback instances) can be invoked during these maintenance windows, and if so what the SLA posture will be while the customer controls the primary infra?
- If failback is not automatic, what telemetry and runbook steps do you require for a graceful handback and for attributing uptime/latency during the window?
- We attached our maintenance plan and would appreciate any required config changes on your side.

We anticipate the customer will want a written carveout or an exception letter clarifying uptime exclusions tied to these maintenance windows. Please advise who at Redwood should review that request and an expected turnaround for a redline.

Thanks,
Radial Bio Ops Team
(operations lead: Thomas Lee)

Attachments: radial-maintenance-plan.pdf
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Ops Team (Radial Bio) <ops@radial.bio>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Scheduled maintenance windows + failback expectations

Hi Thomas / Radial Ops,

Thanks for the heads up and for attaching the maintenance plan. Short answers up front:
- We can support an engineered failback to Redwood-hosted capacity during customer-run maintenance, but it isn't automatic by default for private deployments.
- For SLA attribution during customer maintenance windows, we typically issue a limited exception that excludes the customer-controlled maintenance period from Redwood uptime calculations provided the customer has followed the agreed change notice and runbook.

Action items I propose:
1) Marcus (tech) and I will review the maintenance plan and produce a concrete handback matrix showing conditions we need to trigger failback (health checks, KV-cache warmup, prefix cache warmup timelines).
2) Kimberley (AE) — can you prepare a draft exception letter that limits the exclusion to the announced windows and references our monitored handback checklist?
3) Thomas — please confirm whether your maintenance includes network topology changes or only host patching; if network changes are in scope we will need a 72h lead time.

Let's aim for a short sync early next week. If you want to share the change board ticket/link I can loop Legal for a quick redline.

Best,
David
David Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Ops Team (Radial Bio) <ops@radial.bio>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Scheduled maintenance windows + failback expectations

David / Thomas — quick technical clarifications and suggested handback_matrix attached (service-handback-matrix.xlsx).

Summary of technical constraints:
- Failback prerequisites: active KV cache snapshot OR a warmed prefix cache within 30 minutes of cutover; otherwise first-request latency will spike as caches refill.
- Networking: if Radial modifies BGP sessions or performs switch-level firmware upgrades that alter pathing, the window should be treated as a network-impacting maintenance and will require 72 hours notice.
- Monitoring: Redwood requires the following signals during the window to accept the exclusion:
  * health.p95_token_latency (pre-window baseline vs during-window)
  * error.rate (5m) for token emitters
  * explicit change ticket ID from Radial ops

On SLA attribution: we can offer a written exception that excludes "planned customer-controlled maintenance windows" from SLA calculations provided:
1) Radial publishes the windows to the shared change board at least 7 days in advance (we can accept 72h for urgent security fixes);
2) Radial provides the ticket ID and a post-maintenance incident report for any unplanned degradation;
3) The customer accepts that failback will likely incur a warmup period (typical 10-45 minutes) where latency may exceed our standard SLO.

I attached the handback matrix with specific checks and suggested runbook steps. If possible please indicate which hosts will be patched so we can pre-warm cache on the fallback fleet.

--Marcus
Marcus Lin
Infrastructure Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: service-handback-matrix.xlsx
From: Thomas Lee <tlee@radial.bio>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Scheduled maintenance windows + failback expectations

David / Marcus — thanks for the fast response and the matrix.

A few follow-ups from our side:
- These windows are host patching only; we are not changing BGP or peering during the announced windows. 72h notice is fine for anything that would be network-impacting.
- We can publish the change tickets to the shared Drive and will provide post-maint reports for any unexpected issues.
- The customer has asked for a formal exception letter to be added to the contract that:
  1) Explicitly excludes announced customer-maintenance windows from the uptime calculation;
  2) Requires Redwood to publish the expected warmup latency range and an engineering contact for escalations during the window.

Can you confirm Redwood's earliest delivery target for the exception redline? Our internal procurement needs a signed document before the next board meeting (2027-03-25).

If you prefer to draft the redline first we can take a look and return comments within 48 hours. Otherwise, please propose an SLA carveout text and we'll route it to procurement.

Thanks,
Thomas
Radial Bio — Ops Lead
